blocks.alt: Industrial automation maintenance and technical support

blocks.html: Ensuring continuous operation of a production line depends on the control system staying available. One of the most significant threats is a failure inside the control system. Maintenance is essential for mitigating that risk, whether scheduled, preventive or corrective. A planned maintenance strategy reduces production slowdowns and complete stoppages from DCS, ESD or historian faults.
On-site and remote support for control systems already running in production.

items.html: Improve process performance while reducing costs
Extend the service life of installed systems

blocks.html: Maintenance work is targeted and condition-based: improve the efficiency, reliability and service life of your automation systems by acting on measured condition rather than on a calendar alone.

Effective maintenance starts with an audit of systems and devices. Using accurate and up-to-date condition data, we identify the actions required, when and where they apply, and eliminate unnecessary tasks. That audit also supports predictive maintenance — reducing the risk of unexpected failures. On the refinery CHP plant we have maintained DCS, ESD, BMS and MES continuously since 2022, and for eleven years before that from 2007 to 2018.
Alongside condition-based maintenance, we implement the calculations that show whether a plant is performing as designed:

items.html: Boiler efficiency by direct and indirect method, for gas-fired and petroleum coke fired circulating fluidized bed boilers
Thermal balances and electrical energy balances
Process data collection from control systems and commercial metering units, with long-term archiving

blocks.html: Control loop performance is monitored continuously, loops are retuned, and alternative control strategies are implemented where the existing one limits the unit.
